title: Relationships: One‑to‑Many and Many‑to‑One
description: Model associations between entities with @OneToMany and @ManyToOne.

slides.title: Why Relationships Matter 🔗
slides.content:
# Real‑World Models

Entities rarely live in isolation. A `User` can have many `Order`s – that's a **one‑to‑many** relationship. Conversely, many orders belong to one user – **many‑to‑one**.

In JPA, we annotate the relationship fields with `@OneToMany` and `@ManyToOne`.

quizData.question: If a User can have many Orders, which annotation should be placed on the `orders` field in the User entity?
quizData.explanation: @OneToMany is used on the side that holds the collection of related entities.

Understanding `mappedBy` and Cascade 🔄
slides.content:
# Bidirectional Relationship

* `mappedBy = "user"` – tells JPA that the `Order` entity owns the relationship (it contains the foreign key). The `User` side is the inverse.
* `cascade = CascadeType.ALL` – means operations (persist, merge, remove, etc.) on a `User` will be cascaded to its `Order`s. For example, saving a user will also save its orders.
* `orphanRemoval = true` – if an order is removed from the list, it will be deleted from the database.

slides.title: Lazy vs Eager Loading 🐢⚡
slides.content: By default, `@OneToMany` is **lazy** – the collection is loaded only when accessed. `@ManyToOne` is **eager** – the related entity is loaded immediately. You can change this with `fetch = FetchType.LAZY` or `EAGER`.
